deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (previous page). Hilbert studies Q(x) = X_n(α) X_{n+1}(x) − X_{n+1}(α) X_n(x), where X_n is the Legendre polynomial. Q is the combination of two consecutive Legendre polynomials that vanishes at x = α. Up to a factor, Q/(x−α) is the Christoffel–Darboux kernel K_n(x,α). He showed Q satisfies a linear second-order ODE with singular points ±1, a and ∞ (Heun type), containing a parameter a and an accessory parameter λ.

PART 1: Q as a continued-fraction denominator.
Hilbert wants to characterize Q intrinsically, 'like the Kugelfunktion', once a is given. The Legendre analogue is the classical fact that ∫ dx/((1−x²)X_n²) has no logarithmic terms at the zeros of X_n. That fact gives Legendre's second-kind function Q_n = X_n·∫…, hence the Padé denominators of log((1+x)/(1−x)).

Requirement: Q is a polynomial of degree n+1 such that
 ∫ (x−a)/((x²−1) Q(x)²) dx = A log(x−1) + B log(x+1) + R(x), with R rational.
This means all residues at the zeros of Q vanish. (The written "B'(x'+1)" means B·log(x'+1).)

Residues at the endpoints [explicit computation mine]:
- A = Res_{x=1} = (1−a)/(2 Q(1)²).
- B = Res_{x=−1} = (1+a)/(2 Q(−1)²).

No log at infinity: the integrand is O(x^{−2n−3}), so its integral is O(x^{−2n−2}) with no log term. The residue theorem then forces A + B = 0, i.e.
 (1−a)/Q(1)² + (1+a)/Q(−1)² = 0.
Hence Q(1)²/Q(−1)² = −(1−a)/(1+a) = (a−1)/(a+1), so Q(1):Q(−1) is a given number determined by a.

Conclusion: the Q are exactly the denominators of rational approximations Z/Q to log((1+x)/(1−x)) under the side condition that Q(+1):Q(−1) has a prescribed value. In modern terms these are constrained Padé denominators, i.e. quasi-orthogonal polynomials. The underlying mechanism is the second solution of the ODE: Q·∫ W/Q² with Wronskian W ∝ (x−a)/(x²−1) equals (const)·Q·log((x−1)/(x+1)) + rational.

Consistency check [mine]:
- Q(1) = X_n(α) − X_{n+1}(α) and Q(−1) = (−1)^{n+1}(X_n(α) + X_{n+1}(α)).
- Solving the endpoint relation gives a = (ρ + 1/ρ)/2 with ρ = X_{n+1}(α)/X_n(α). So |a| ≥ 1, as reality of Q(1)/Q(−1) requires.
- For n = 0 (Q = x − α), vanishing of the residue at x = α gives exactly a = (1+α²)/(2α).

PART 2: expansion in the P_n.
The P_n (defined on his p. 66) are presumably the polynomials vanishing at α:
 P_n(x) = X_{n+1}(x)/X_{n+1}(α) − X_n(x)/X_n(α).
The claim is that not every analytic f can be expanded in them.

Step 1 [verified, mine]. Expand f(x)/(x−α) = Σ c_n X_n(x) in Legendre polynomials. The three-term recurrence, applied at x and at α, gives
 (2n+1)(x−α) X_n(x) = F_n := (n+1) X_{n+1}(α) P_n(x) − n X_{n−1}(α) P_{n−1}(x).
This is the 'Formel S. 81'; Hilbert writes (x−α)X_n = F, omitting the factor 2n+1.

Step 2. Then f = Σ c_n F_n/(2n+1). Regrouping by Abel summation gives a formal 'Fourier' expansion f = Σ d_n P_n with
 d_n = (n+1) X_{n+1}(α) c_n/(2n+1) − (n+1) X_n(α) c_{n+1}/(2n+3).

Step 3. The regrouping is legitimate only if the boundary term ~ c_N N X_{N−1}(α) P_{N−1}(x) tends to 0. Hilbert first writes this as lim X_{n−1}(α)/X_n(α) = 0. He then argues that for α in (−1,1), α can be chosen so that the quotient misbehaves (X_n(α) is near zero along a subsequence), so the limit condition fails and the expansion cannot represent f.

Step 4. The last line, written below the rule, retracts this: the quotient X_{n−1}(α)/X_n(α) 'does not oscillate between −∞ and +∞ as strongly as needed!' So the non-expandability argument is acknowledged by Hilbert himself to be inconclusive.

The bottom lines spell out F explicitly in terms of the normalized differences X_{n+1}(x)/X_{n+1}(α) − X_n(x)/X_n(α).
errors: Sign slip: A + B = 0 gives Q(1)²/Q(−1)² = −(1−a)/(1+a), so Q(1)/Q(−1) = ±sqrt((a−1)/(a+1)), not sqrt((1−a)/(1+a)). The written version is imaginary for the relevant |a| > 1.
The asymptotic written as a/x'^{…+2} is only schematic. The leading term of the integral is ~ −x^{−2n−2}/((2n+2)·lc(Q)²); only the absence of a log term matters, and that is correct.
Formula 'S.81' as written, (x−α)X_n = F, lacks the factor 1/(2n+1): actually (2n+1)(x−α)X_n(x) = F_n.

The non-expandability argument is not established. The convergence condition is stated loosely (the boundary term also involves c_n and P_{n−1}(x)), and Hilbert himself retracts the argument in the final line. As it stands, the claim that not every analytic f is expandable in the P_n is unproved on this page.

The phrase 'X_n(α) stärker als X_{n−1}(α) unendlich wird' cannot be literal for fixed α in (−1,1), since |X_n(α)| ≤ 1. The intended phenomenon is presumably smallness of X_n(α), i.e. growth of 1/X_n(α) or of the quotient.

results.what: Characterization of Q = X_n(α)X_{n+1}(x) − X_{n+1}(α)X_n(x) as the degree-(n+1) polynomial for which ∫(x−a)/((x²−1)Q²)dx has logarithms only at ±1, with the side condition (1−a)/Q(1)² + (1+a)/Q(−1)² = 0 from absence of a log at infinity.
results.modern_name: Quasi-orthogonal polynomials / Christoffel–Darboux kernel polynomials. Second solution via the Wronskian (reduction of order) for a Heun-type equation. Residue theorem at infinity.
results.usually_credited_to: Christoffel (kernel polynomials, 1858); M. Riesz (1923), Shohat (1937), Chihara (1957) for quasi-orthogonality. The Legendre analogue (no log terms in ∫dx/((1−x²)P_n²)) is classical (Legendre, Heine, Christoffel).

results.what: Q as denominators of rational approximations Z/Q to log((1+x)/(1−x)) with a prescribed ratio Q(1):Q(−1).
results.modern_name: Constrained Padé approximation / continued-fraction denominators of the Legendre function Q_0. Quasi-orthogonal Padé denominators.
results.usually_credited_to: Legendre function Q_n and continued fraction: Gauss, Heine, Christoffel. Padé (1892) for the general theory.

results.what: Identity (2n+1)(x−α)X_n(x) = (n+1)X_{n+1}(α)P_n(x) − nX_{n−1}(α)P_{n−1}(x), with P_n = X_{n+1}(x)/X_{n+1}(α) − X_n(x)/X_n(α). It is used to convert a Legendre expansion of f/(x−α) into an expansion of f in the P_n.
results.modern_name: Consequence of the Legendre three-term recurrence (Bonnet). Abel summation and expansions in non-orthogonal (quasi-orthogonal) polynomial systems.
results.usually_credited_to: Bonnet / Legendre recurrence (classical); expansion technique is folklore.

results.what: Attempted (and self-retracted) argument that not every analytic function admits a convergent expansion in the P_n.
results.modern_name: Completeness/convergence of expansions in quasi-orthogonal or kernel polynomial systems.

deep.surprise_reason: Competent working notes on classical material: Legendre polynomials, combinations vanishing at a point, residue arguments, and Padé denominators of log((1+x)/(1−x)). This anticipates the later formal notion of quasi-orthogonal polynomials and of Heun-type equations for them. However, the ingredients (Christoffel kernels, Legendre's second-kind functions, continued fractions) were all well known by c. 1908–1910. The one non-routine claim (non-expandability) is retracted by Hilbert himself.

checkable.asserts: Res_{x=1} (x−a)/((x²−1)Q²) = (1−a)/(2Q(1)²); the Q factor is set aside here and the check gives 0.

checkable.sympy: x,al=symbols('x alpha'); n=3; P=lambda k: legendre(k,x)/legendre(k,al); F=(n+1)*legendre(n+1,al)*(P(n+1)-P(n)) - n*legendre(n-1,al)*(P(n)-P(n-1)); simplify(F - (2*n+1)*(x-al)*legendre(n,x))
checkable.asserts: Formula 'S.81' with the corrected factor: F_n = (2n+1)(x−α)X_n(x). Should simplify to 0; repeat for other n.
For n=0 (Q = x−α), the residue at the zero of Q vanishes exactly when a = (1+α²)/(2α) = (ρ+1/ρ)/2 with ρ = X_1(α)/X_0(α). Should give 0.

checkable.sympy: x,al=symbols('x alpha'); n=1; Q=legendre(n,al)*legendre(n+1,x)-legendre(n+1,al)*legendre(n,x); rho=legendre(n+1,al)/legendre(n,al); a=(rho+1/rho)/2; g=(x-a)/((x**2-1)*Q**2); [simplify(residue(g,x,r)) for r in solve(Q,x)]
checkable.asserts: Conjectured: with a = (ρ+1/ρ)/2, the integrand has zero residue at every zero of Q, so the integral has logs only at ±1. Expected all 0; this is the page's defining property.

checkable.sympy: al=symbols('alpha'); n=2; Q1=legendre(n,al)-legendre(n+1,al); Qm1=(-1)**(n+1)*(legendre(n,al)+legendre(n+1,al)); rho=legendre(n+1,al)/legendre(n,al); a=(rho+1/rho)/2; simplify((1-a)/Q1**2+(1+a)/Qm1**2)
checkable.asserts: The endpoint condition A+B=0 holds for a = (ρ+1/ρ)/2. Should give 0.
With u = Q(1)²/Q(−1)², A+B=0 gives u = (a−1)/(a+1), confirming the sign slip in Hilbert's sqrt((1−a)/(1+a)). Should give 0.

Denominators in both integrals should be (x'²−1)Q², not 'x'^2-1 Q^2'.
'{+sowieso+} dann [?]' reads 'offenbar sowieso für x' = ∞ …', with 'sowieso' inserted above the line.

In 'Formel S. 81 (x'−α) X_n'' the prime is on the argument x', i.e. X_n(x'), not a derivative. The crossed-out fraction terms are (n+1)P_{n+1}/X_{n+1}(α) and nP_{n-1}/X_{n-1}(α)-type terms, struck and replaced by F.
The inserted phrase reads 'wenn man dann α geeignet wählt' (inserted above 'einrichten').
Last line should read 'schwankt nicht zwischen −∞ und +∞ so stark, als nötig!'; the word 'zwischen' is missing from the transcription.
